In English, a single gerund phrase, as t.why: Held as a usage pattern seen hundreds of thousands of times ('Swimming is' 180,781 and 'Smoking is' 319,409 times in Dolma) and as a rule stated in grammar teaching. It could also be derived (a gerund phrase is a singular noun phrase; a singular subject takes a singular verb), but the pattern is so frequent that it is rated stored (unlikely) and no premises are listed. Bare plural forms ('Swimming are') are not counted: they are dominated by lists and coordinations. The fixed phrases of queries 3 and 4 are counted against their plural-verb versions. 'Reading books are' (1,704) is the noun-phrase reading ('Reading books are checked every Wednesday', books for reading) in the hits sampled, against 11,599 for 'Reading books is'.

sources.quote: A gerund phrase as a subject is always treated as ONE unit — it takes a singular verb!

notes: An agreement rule not used before in this topic (0005 names of one person, 0006 mass nouns). Restricted to a single gerund phrase as the subject of an ordinary present-tense statement: two gerunds joined by 'and' ('Buying and flipping houses is/are') vary between singular and plural and are kept out of every prompt (R1). The phrase 'Collecting old coins' in the paraphrase and cross-lingual queries contains a plural noun on purpose: the verb still agrees with the gerund. Determinate queries use verbs invented for the prompt ('snorve', 'dramp'; Dolma 0 and 2 hits), and the prompt says each is a verb, so its -ing form as subject is a gerund and the rule is the only route. World structure (coordinator's rule, README Decisions 2): in a world where a fixed phrase is stored whole, the phrase's class membership gives way and it falls under a wider, unedited rule that still gives the original form; it never stands as an exception to the edited rule, which would be the inconsistent patch. The two phrases are independent storage choices, so four worlds. Under delete, the wider rule would re-derive the deleted one, so the delete record's worlds also cut the class's link to it (README, Delete under determinacy: the wider rule itself cannot go, being anchored by countless instances outside the chain). In the stored worlds 'Smoking' and 'Parting' are read as plain nouns rather than gerunds: dictionaries list 'smoking' (the habit) and 'parting' (leave-taking) as nouns, and a bare -ing word with no object or modifier is exactly where the gerund and noun readings meet, so the membership can really give way; as a mass noun ('smoking') and a singular noun ('parting') they still take a singular verb. The edit's definition of a gerund phrase (an -ing form used as a noun while still acting as a verb, able to take an object or an adverb) is what lets these bare forms leave the class without also taking the edit's own examples ('Swimming every day', 'Reading books') with them; the determinate queries give their invented gerunds an object or an adverb ('dramping the dough', 'snorving quietly') so no plain-noun reading is open. 'Seeing is believing' was considered and dropped: 'seeing' has no natural plain-noun reading there. Agreement compares the verb's number with the subject's: fol. Forced-choice questions throughout. Near unrelated: an irregular plural ('geese'), whose answer is not 'are'.
